turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: For about three weeks I’ve been feeling very fatigued and having trouble concentrating. I also get short of breath with exertion, feel dizzy at times, and my fingers ache and improve when I keep them cold.

I’m sorry you’re feeling this way. One question to start: **have you noticed any bleeding or bruising more than usual** (e.g., nose/gum bleeding, blood in stool/urine, heavy periods, or easy bruises)?
Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any unusual bleeding or bruising—no blood in my stool or urine, and nothing like frequent nose or gum bleeding.
Thanks. Next question: **Have you had any fevers, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss during these three weeks?**
Patient: No fevers, no night sweats, and I haven’t had any unintentional weight loss. I just feel weak and short of breath when I exert myself, and the dizziness comes and goes.
Understood. Next question: **Do you have any chest pain, palpitations (feeling your heart racing/irregular), or fainting episodes?**

Patient: I haven’t had chest pain, but I do sometimes notice my heart beating a bit harder or faster, and I haven’t fainted. The main issues are getting short of breath with exertion and feeling lightheaded at times.
Got it. Next question: **Have you had any recent infections or new medications (including chemotherapy, antibiotics, or supplements), or any known blood disorders?**
No recent infections, and I haven’t started any new medications or supplements—just my usual enalapril for hypertension. I don’t have any known blood disorders either.
Thanks. Next question: **When you say your fingers ache and improve when kept cold—do you also notice color changes (white/blue/red) in the fingers with cold or stress, or numbness/tingling?**

Doctor: When your fingers ache and improve with cold, do you also notice color changes like white or blue (or red) with cold or stress, and any numbness or tingling? Patient: Yes—when I’m cold or stressed, my fingers can turn pale or bluish, and they feel sore; I also get some numbness/tingling along with the pain.
That’s helpful. Next question: **Do you have any skin rash, mouth ulcers, or joint swelling/pain (especially in the hands/wrists), or trouble swallowing/heartburn?**

Doctor: Do you have any skin rash, mouth ulcers, joint swelling or pain (especially in the hands or wrists), or trouble swallowing/heartburn? Patient: No rash or mouth ulcers, and I haven’t noticed any obvious joint swelling. I do sometimes feel a bit of heartburn, but I haven’t had trouble swallowing.
Next question: **Have you noticed any shortness of breath at rest, coughing, or swelling in your legs/ankles?**
Patient: No, I’m not short of breath at rest and I don’t really have a cough. I haven’t noticed swelling in my legs or ankles either—mostly the breathing trouble is when I’m exerting myself.
Next question: **Do you have a history of anemia, kidney disease, thyroid disease, or heavy menstrual bleeding (if applicable)?**

Doctor: Do you have a history of anemia, kidney disease, thyroid disease, or heavy menstrual bleeding (if applicable)? Patient: I don’t have a known history of anemia, kidney disease, or thyroid problems, and since I’m a man there’s no menstrual bleeding.
Next question: **Have you had any recent lab tests (CBC, iron studies, thyroid tests) or do you know your hemoglobin/platelet counts?**
Patient: I haven’t had any lab tests recently, and I don’t know my hemoglobin or platelet counts. I haven’t had thyroid testing either.
Next question: **Any headaches, vision changes, or neurologic symptoms (weakness on one side, trouble speaking), or is it mainly fatigue/lightheadedness?**
Patient: Mostly it’s fatigue and getting lightheaded, not headaches or vision changes. I don’t have weakness on one side, trouble speaking, or other neurologic symptoms.
Next question: **Do you have any known heart disease or family history of heart problems, blood clots, or autoimmune diseases?**

Doctor: Do you have any known heart disease or family history of heart problems, blood clots, or autoimmune diseases? Patient: I don’t know of any heart disease in my family, and I’m not aware of blood clots or autoimmune conditions either. I just have my high blood pressure, and I’ve been dealing with these new symptoms for the last few weeks.

I’m going to ask one last focused question: **Have you noticed your fingers turning pale/blue specifically with cold or stress (Raynaud-type episodes), and do you have any ulcers or sores on your fingertips?**
Patient: Yes, when it’s cold or I’m stressed they turn pale or bluish, and they get sore with numbness or tingling. I haven’t noticed any sores or ulcers on my fingertips.
